title: Finite-free exterior frames and internal dual evaluation on a trivializing open
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and M a sheaf of modules. Use its internal dual M^∨ [def-pur-sheaf-hom] and sheafified exterior powers [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power]. Suppose M restricted to U is the free sheaf of rank r [def-weil-pbc-free-module], and V ⊆ U. Set R=O_X(V) and I={s ⊆ Fin(r) : |s|=n}, with each s enumerated increasingly. There exist an R-basis a of M(V) indexed by Fin(r), internal dual sections φ_j satisfying φ_j(x)=a.coord_j(x), an I-indexed R-basis b of (∧ⁿ M^∨)(V) whose s-vector is the wedge of the φ_j for j∈s, an I-indexed R-basis d of (∧ⁿ M)(V) whose s-vector is the wedge of the a_j for j∈s, and an R-linear equivalence c from (∧ⁿ M)^∨(V) to Hom_R((∧ⁿ M)(V),R) given by evaluation at the identity open. No determinant-pairing morphism is part of the hypotheses or conclusion.

proof.text: Restrict the finite free isomorphism along V → U. Its restricted generators identify sections on every smaller open W with O_X(W)^r. On V these are a basis a. A functional with coefficients in O_X(V) extends to the localized sheaf by restricting the coefficients and applying them to the restricted generators; conversely a sheaf morphism is determined by those generators. Applying this to the coordinate functionals gives the internal dual sections φ and their evaluation formula.

The sectionwise exterior presheaves of the trivial sheaf and its dual are finite products of O_X, with basis indexed by increasing n-element subsets. The exterior basis restriction formulas commute with the restrictions of O_X, so these presheaves are sheaves. Their restriction to the localized site is identified with the restriction of their global sheafification by the universal property: smaller-open covers are the same covers in the localized site. Thus the sheafification units carry the two increasing wedge families to bases b and d. This includes the empty index family for n>r and the single empty wedge for n=0.

For the now finite free exterior sheaf, repeat coordinate reconstruction on its restricted wedge basis d. Evaluation of a localized morphism at the identity open is a linear equivalence c to the ring-linear dual of the sections; its inverse uses the values on d as coefficients of a natural sheaf morphism. The two composites are identities because they agree on every restricted basis vector. This constructs exactly the evaluation equivalence claimed, without using any exterior dual pairing map.

theorem exterior_dual_local_frames (X : Scheme.{u}) (M : X.Modules) (n : ℕ)
    (U : X.Opens) (r : ℕ)
    (e : M.over U ≅ SheafOfModules.free (ULift.{u} (Fin r)))
    (V : X.Opens) (g : V ⟶ U) :
    ∃ (a : Module.Basis (Fin r) (X.presheaf.obj (op V)) (M.val.obj (op V)))
      (φ : Fin r → (Scheme.Modules.dual M).val.obj (op V))
      (b : Module.Basis (Set.powersetCard (Fin r) n) (X.presheaf.obj (op V))
        ((Scheme.Modules.exteriorSheaf (Scheme.Modules.dual M) n).val.obj (op V)))
      (d : Module.Basis (Set.powersetCard (Fin r) n) (X.presheaf.obj (op V))
        ((Scheme.Modules.exteriorSheaf M n).val.obj (op V)))
      (c : (Scheme.Modules.dual (Scheme.Modules.exteriorSheaf M n)).val.obj (op V) ≃ₗ[
        X.presheaf.obj (op V)] Module.Dual (X.presheaf.obj (op V))
          ((Scheme.Modules.exteriorSheaf M n).val.obj (op V))),
      (∀ (j : Fin r) (x : M.val.obj (op V)),
        (φ j).app (op (Over.mk (𝟙 V))) x = a.coord j x) ∧
      (∀ s, b s = Scheme.Modules.exteriorSheafSection (Scheme.Modules.dual M) n V
        (φ ∘ Set.powersetCard.ofFinEmbEquiv.symm s)) ∧
      (∀ s, d s = Scheme.Modules.exteriorSheafSection M n V
        (a ∘ Set.powersetCard.ofFinEmbEquiv.symm s)) ∧
      (∀ (ψ : (Scheme.Modules.dual (Scheme.Modules.exteriorSheaf M n)).val.obj (op V))
        (x : (Scheme.Modules.exteriorSheaf M n).val.obj (op V)),
        c ψ x = ψ.app (op (Over.mk (𝟙 V))) x)
